$comment: Strict hierarchy of section-separation methods. Replaces the peer-equal listing in data/v3_2/section_separation_recipes.json for v5-and-later gate decisions.

hierarchy.description: Vertical rhythm alone. Increase inter-section space until the boundary reads.
hierarchy.use_when: the default; almost always sufficient when the type scale has range
hierarchy.risk: requires type scale with real contrast; will fail if hierarchy is flat

hierarchy.description: Column count, alignment axis, content mode, or focal-point changes.
hierarchy.use_when: next section runs on a different rhythm than the current one
hierarchy.risk: random zig-zag if unmotivated; each shift needs a reason

hierarchy.description: Chapter marker, scale change, weight change, or role change.
hierarchy.use_when: next section changes mode (from prose to reference, from marketing to data)
hierarchy.risk: eyebrow spam if used per section; AF-E03 fires

hierarchy.description: Two tonally distinct surfaces meet at the boundary. A real edge.
hierarchy.use_when: functional mode change or brand-signaled chapter
hierarchy.risk: striped page if every section changes; commit to real difference or drop it

hierarchy.use_when: visual narrative changes; media is a natural chapter break
hierarchy.risk: media used as filler rather than as a real image

hierarchy.use_when: the composition is restructuring for a new content shape
hierarchy.risk: unmotivated shift reads as broken layout

hierarchy.use_when: priorities 1-6 have been considered and rejected with a documented reason, AND the divider is part of the brand's editorial language, AND it appears rarely with authored weight and length
hierarchy.risk: single most-recognized AI fingerprint (AF-A01); requires justification field

justification_schema.comprehension_gain: string; what the reader now understands

hard_blockers.pattern: full-width horizontal rule between every section
hard_blockers.action: delete every instance; rework whitespace, type scale, or surface

hard_blockers.pattern: global page grid overlay for atmosphere
hard_blockers.action: delete; do not replace with alternative atmosphere device

hard_blockers.pattern: hairline card borders on dark surfaces
hard_blockers.action: see COMPOSITION_RESTRAINT.md; either commit to real containment or remove the container

hard_blockers.pattern: decorative technical lines around empty areas
hard_blockers.action: delete unless the interface is genuinely about measurement

hard_blockers.pattern: repeated border-bottom on stacked list items outside of dense tabular data
hard_blockers.action: use spacing or alternating surface instead
delete; underlines belong to interactive text, not labels
